note: External documentation this project's decisions depend on. Read the source before answering anything version-dependent — see .claude/rules/model-integrity.md. Every entry says why we come here; an entry nobody can justify should be deleted rather than kept 'for reference'. 'version' is the range installed here (pnpm-lock.yaml has the resolved one); 'checked' is when the link was last confirmed to resolve.

prisma-client-extensions.why: The auto-scoping extension (ADR-005) is our replacement for RLS, so its exact boundary matters more than its features: query extensions intercept the model API and do NOT intercept $queryRaw / $executeRaw, and they see top-level operations only — a nested write keeps whatever userId the caller put on the nested rows. Confirm the boundary here before claiming anything is scoped automatically. Three things measured in F1.3 that the page does not spell out: a free-standing Prisma.defineExtension loses the schema's type map (every args degrades to never — write it as client.$extends instead); a named per-operation hook and $allOperations both run, the named one outermost, so a catch-all cannot simply throw; and the extension holds inside $transaction, on the transactional client too. Unrelated but measured on the same CLI: `migrate dev --help` claims it triggers generators, and it does not — always run `pnpm --filter @rondo/db build` after a migration.

node-async-local-storage.why: The request context (F1.3) is hand-written on AsyncLocalStorage rather than nestjs-cls (the workspace pins node >=26 in engines, .nvmrc and every CI job), so its semantics are ours to know: a store is shared by everything in one async chain, propagates across await, and is absent in anything that escapes the request (timers, event listeners, background work). Come here before assuming a value survives into code the request did not await.

clerk-authorized-parties.why: verifyToken() is configured with authorizedParties, so a session token is accepted only when its azp claim equals WEB_ORIGIN (F1.3). The installed SDK rejects a token whose azp is missing entirely, not just mismatched — which is why every api test that mints a token has to set the claim.

prisma-raw-queries.why: Raw aggregates (balance, RTA, Available) are the one place the extension cannot protect. Come here for parameterisation and the difference between $queryRaw and $queryRawUnsafe before writing SQL that carries userId / budgetId by hand.

eslint-no-restricted-syntax.why: The lint rule that keeps $queryRaw / $executeRaw out of everything except the context-aware repository is what makes ADR-005 enforceable in CI. Selector syntax and message wiring live here.

eslint-no-restricted-imports.why: Layer boundaries from ADR-002 (web never imports Prisma; DTOs come from packages/types) are enforced as import restrictions rather than left to review.

clerk-manual-jwt-verification.version: @clerk/nextjs ^7.7.1, @clerk/backend ^3.16.6 (a direct dependency of apps/api since F1.2)
clerk-manual-jwt-verification.why: The NestJS guard verifies the Clerk JWT itself and puts userId into the request context — the first link in the isolation chain. Networkless verification, the JWKS cache and which claim actually holds the user id are all version-dependent. One trap the page does not spell out: jwtKey takes the PEM public key and @clerk/backend derives the JWK from it by string surgery on the 2048-bit RSA SPKI prefix, so a key of any other size silently fails to load.

clerk-session-tokens.why: Token lifetime and what happens to a revoked session: a signed-out or banned user keeps a technically valid token until it expires. Know the size of that window before writing anything about sign-out being immediate.

railway-config-as-code.why: apps/*/railway.json owns every build and deploy setting Railway lets config-as-code own, watch paths included (F1.13); variables, domains and the repository binding stay in the UI. A key that does not exist is ignored in silence: a typo in watchPatterns stops real deploys, or lets a migration-only commit through unnoticed. Confirm the key name and its section against this reference or the schema (https://backboard.railway.app/railway.schema.json) before editing either file — never from memory.

railway-watch-paths.why: The pattern syntax behind build.watchPatterns: gitignore-style, always anchored at the repository root even when a Root Directory is set, and negation only after an including rule. Both images build from the repo root, so these patterns decide whether a packages/db migration ever reaches dev — see docs/deploy-railway.md.

iso-4217-currency-codes.why: SIX is the ISO 4217 maintenance agency and publishes the authoritative code list with each currency's minor-unit exponent. Money is minor units in bigint and the digit count comes from the currency, never a hardcoded 2 — so this list, not intuition, decides how a budget's amounts are parsed and rendered. Readable summary: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217
